g.text: Augmented GRU with learned feature encoders
Candidate g112 | representative seed 3 (lowest validation loss) | restored epoch 18 | 40,945 parameter entries
A Encode inputs available before response t
Log(1 + student time gap in seconds)
Concatenate: 16 time + 16 history + 16 item + 16 skill = 64 coordinates
Input dropout 0.1 produces x(t), shared by prediction and memory update
Each encoder has its own weights and biases. Its 16-value output is linear; ReLU is applied after the 32-unit hidden layer.
The current answer is still unknown here. The head reads the previous top-layer memory, just as in the original model.
C Observe and encode the answer, then update memory
Retain all three states for the next trial: [h1(t), h2(t), h3(t)] = 3 × 32 values
Each new participant starts with zero memory. Updated memory affects the next prediction, p(t+1).
All encoders, embeddings, GRU layers and head weights are learned jointly by backpropagation; continuation keeps weights fixed.
Encoder dropout is zero. Input, between-GRU-layer and head dropout are 0.1 during training and disabled during evaluation.
D Changes from the original augmented GRU figure
The GRU remains 3 × 32. There is no separate student-inference network, Gaussian sampling, or KL penalty in this model.
New encoder blocks are amber. Exact dimensions, equations and held-out predictions verified against the saved LKT 2.0.0.9011 checkpoint.
